content_html:
There are several real ways to get to Machu Picchu today, and each offers a different experience in terms of comfort, adventure, time, and budget.

Choosing the right route can completely improve your trip.

That’s why here we explain the main ways to get to Machu Picchu in 2026 and which one is best depending on your travel style.

1. Reaching Machu Picchu by Train

The most comfortable and popular option

Most international travelers arrive by train.

Typical route:

  • Transfer from Cusco or the Sacred Valley to the train station
  • Train to Aguas Calientes
  • Official shuttle bus to Machu Picchu entrance (approx. 25–30 min)

Ideal for:

  • Families
  • Travelers with limited time
  • Those seeking comfort

Advantages:

  • Fastest and most comfortable route
  • Spectacular scenery during the journey
  • No physical effort required

Disadvantages:

  • Most expensive option
  • Best train schedules often sell out in advance

2. The Inca Trail

The most iconic trekking route

The Inca Trail remains the most legendary way to reach Machu Picchu.

Popular options:

  • Classic Inca Trail (4 days)
  • Short Inca Trail (2 days)

Ideal for:

  • Trekking enthusiasts
  • Adventure travelers
  • Those seeking a complete historical experience

Advantages:

  • Arrive on foot through the historic Sun Gate
  • Unique cultural and natural experience
  • Considered one of the world’s best hikes

Disadvantages:

  • Requires good physical condition
  • Limited to approximately 500 permits per day including staff
  • Must be booked several months in advance
  • Closed every February for maintenance and conservation

3. Hydroelectric Route

The budget-friendly alternative

This is the cheapest way to get to Machu Picchu.

How it works:

  • Ground transportation to Hydroelectric Station
  • Approx. 2–3 hour walk along the railway to Aguas Calientes

Ideal for:

  • Backpackers
  • Budget travelers
  • Adventurous visitors

Advantages:

  • Lower cost
  • Flexible route
  • Alternative experience

Disadvantages:

  • Longer travel time
  • Less comfortable
  • Requires additional walking

4. Alternative Treks (Salkantay and Others)

For travelers seeking adventure without the Inca Trail

Many travelers choose alternative treks such as:

  • Salkantay Trek
  • Lares Trek
  • Inca Jungle Trek

These routes typically finish in Aguas Calientes before entering Machu Picchu.

Ideal for:

  • Adventure travelers
  • Those who could not secure Inca Trail permits
  • Travelers looking for less regulated trekking routes

Which Option Should You Choose?

If you want comfort:

Train

If you want the classic experience:

Inca Trail

If you want to save money:

Hydroelectric Route

If you want alternative trekking:

Salkantay / Other Treks

Key Factors to Consider Before Choosing

Before deciding, consider:

  • Total budget
  • Available time
  • Physical fitness level
  • Travel season
  • Permit and ticket availability

There is no single best option… only the best one for your travel style.

Why Choosing the Right Route Matters

Because getting to Machu Picchu is not just transportation…

It is a fundamental part of the experience.

How you arrive can completely change how you experience the journey.
